prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which designed small molecules bring a chosen protein to an E3 ubiquitin ligase so that the cell removes it

statement.case_for: I move from B005 to B011. Reading the full round-1 exchange, B005 has the thinnest support on the list (two members ranked it, and the chair notes that efficiencies have plateaued), while B011 is the only item that every member places in a preferred configuration or alternatives list. My own round-1 test was whether structure determines function and whether the mechanism was actually established. B011 meets it better than I credited: a bifunctional molecule forms a defined ternary complex, Ciulli's structures of VHL-ligand and PROTAC-induced ternary complexes showed the cooperativity and protein-protein contacts that make design rational, and the principle has been reproduced across many E3 ligases and target classes in independent laboratories. That is structural evidence, not only phenotype. It also gives a whole community a new capability, which is the kind of enabling achievement I weight most. Crews and Deshaies for the concept and first proof of principle, with Ciulli for structure-guided design, gives an attributable trio around one coherent citation.
statement.case_against: No degrader is yet a broadly approved drug, so the clinical consequence is promised rather than shown, and a prize now could look a few years early; I cannot verify trial outcomes. A trio of Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli leaves out Sakamoto and Kim from the 2001 paper and the molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito, Gray), and the citation will be read as covering both. B005 remains, in my judgement, the more mature and more clearly overdue discovery, with a cleaner two-person credit; I am conceding that to join a plurality position rather than split the vote on a candidate that is unlikely to reach five.

responses.point: Chabes keeps Handa in the trio so that the cereblon identification and the molecular-glue branch are covered, and would accept Ciulli if the majority wants a PROTAC-centred citation.
responses.response: I take the cereblon discovery seriously as a mechanism, but a prize that tries to cover PROTACs and glues in three names will be imprecise whichever name is dropped. From a structural viewpoint, what makes the PROTAC line general is the ternary-complex structures and the cooperativity they explain, and that is Ciulli's contribution. I therefore side with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli and a citation worded on designed recruitment of an E3 ligase, with glues left for a later, separately framed recognition. Since you say you would accept Ciulli in a PROTAC-centred citation, I think we are closer than round 1 suggested.

responses.point: Aili argues that the Crews-Deshaies-Ciulli line is about designing new degraders, that Handa's work explains an existing drug, and that glues, if wanted, deserve a separate part.
responses.response: I agree with the separation, and with your point that a mixed three-name citation is less clean. I do not think a second part is needed now: a two-part prize would force us to credit names we have not examined closely enough, and the glue strand is not yet argued to the same standard. I would keep the citation on the chemical principle, as you suggest, and not on approvals, which answers my own earlier maturity worry as far as it can be answered.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, supports B011 as the strongest case and says he would be content with B005 if B011 stalls on attribution; he also presses that the citation should not claim therapeutic success.
responses.response: I appreciate that you treat B005 as a serious alternative, and on credit I think B011 does not stall: four members already name the same trio or differ only on the third name. I accept your wording constraint, a citation on the principle of recruiting an E3 ligase to remove a chosen protein, with no claim about drugs. To your question to the four B011 supporters, my own answer is that the lack of an approved degrader would trouble me less than an unclear citation; it is the structure and mechanism that I need to see established, and they are.

responses.point: Somfai holds B055 first, keeps B011 as an alternative, says he would not block it if the committee converges, and argues that C-N coupling is chemically distinct from the 2010 prize.
responses.response: Your argument that C-N coupling needed a different mechanistic solution is fair, and I said in round 1 that I would not oppose B055 if the committee judged it worthy. But I still see it as more of an extension than B011, which creates a capability that did not exist, and only two members ranked it. If you hold B055 as a first choice I understand it, but since you list B011 as your first alternative, I would ask you to weigh that it is the one item that can reach five without anyone abandoning a principle.

responses.point: Brzezinski prefers B058 on maturity and mechanistic clarity, and asks that the B011 case separate demonstrated chemistry from expected clinical benefit.
responses.response: I share your request, and my citation is written to meet it: it describes what the molecules do in the cell, not what drugs they will become. On B058 I still think the priority overlap with Marcus, Dutton and Moser, and Beratan and Onuchic is difficult for a narrow citation. I keep B008 as an alternative because you and Chabes find the nitrogenase structures solid; our difference is how the structural evidence is weighed against the open mechanism.

uncertainties: Whether clinical validation of degraders will be sufficient by the announcement; I have not verified trial status.
Whether the committee will want the molecular-glue and cereblon strand reflected, which would put Handa in the trio and omit Ciulli.
Whether Hagfeldt should be added for B005 if the committee turns to it as an alternative, and whether the perovskite lineage changes its weight.
I cannot independently verify the precise credit split in the supplied B011 list, including the contributions of Sakamoto, Kim, Ito and Gray.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for Crews, Deshaies or Ciulli, or for the alternatives B005 and B008. My only listed connection is a Stockholm University colleague relationship with Peter Brzezinski, who is not a candidate; my own work on 3D electron diffraction of porous materials is near structural work in B008 and I note that as subject proximity, not a recusal issue.
